Criminalization with lashing/death penalty, official warnings to trans people to avoid busy areas, custodial rape, forced tests, executions for homosexuality, recognition only via surgery. Official advisory restricting trans presence in public, security forces arresting suspected gay or trans. That's organized state targeting → tier 2. Score 0.12.

Dossier 4: Kuwait-like (Article 199bis struck down 2022). Criminalizes same-sex conduct (Article 193, enforced), dress policing persisted after ruling, no LGR, no protections, film bans, no NGO. But no documented ongoing trans-specific criminalization post-2022; discrimination by officials persists. Severity: arrest under morality/sodomy laws, deportation of HIV+ foreigners. Score ~0.30-0.35. Since cross-dressing law struck down 2022 but police discrimination persists, plus enforced sodomy law which can be leveraged. Also 2017 arrest for looking feminine (before the ruling). I'd say 0.32.

High transfemicide counts (raw counts, no denominators — per rule 16, if only violence content is such a figure treat as undocumented... but there's more: police extortion, documented impunity, official commission warning impunity, rights rarely enforced, murders of activists). Also documented acceptance in places, same-sex marriage everywhere, third-gender tradition, transfemicide law in capital. Violence against trans people is documented pattern with state tolerance/impunity — that's more than raw counts: 2024 reports of killings increasing, protests, impunity warning. But is it above background? Mexico general homicide is very high. Raw counts without denominators carry no magnitude. Hmm. Public hostility not documented as organized targeting; violence is serious but partially background. Documented police extortion of trans people = tier 2-ish but described vaguely ("police corrupt and prone to extortion, transvestites subject to abuse"). Impunity documented. Score 0.50.

Now dossier 1 vs 5: Dossier 1 has tier-1 universal exposures (single-sex code in force, strip-search by birth sex, ward bans, prison placement). But the Joelle case: denial of cancer care leading to death — that's severe, care denial in emergency tier 1. So 0.45.

Dossier 5: violence + impunity but also protections, marriage, transfemicide law, acceptance in capital. Elevated but different. I'd give 0.52.

Dossier 2: reduced risk 0.68. It has prison binary placement (tier 1 only in custody), airport screening complaint, sauna guideline restricting women's saunas by sex characteristics — that's a facility restriction emerging but set by private operators, not statute. Self-ID, equal treatment act, functioning institutions, hate-crime campaign. 0.68 sounds right; maybe 0.70. The airport screening incident and prison placement push down. I'll say 0.68.

Dossier 4: 0.32. Hmm — after 2022 decriminalization of cross-dressing, what's the trans visitor's exposure? Enforced sodomy law (Article 193, 7 years) — but for trans visitors this matters as lever; dress-code policing "outlasted" the ruling per the assessment ("it did not end the dress-code policing that preceded and outlasted it"). Officials discriminate. No protections, no NGO, censorship. Severity: up to imprisonment for same-sex conduct. But no documented trans-specific arrests post-2022. High risk band. 0.30.

Let me set: D1 0.45, D2 0.68, D3 0.12, D4 0.30, D5 0.52.

Per rubric, universal exposure with no working remedy → Elevated band. Both in elevated. D5 slightly higher? Violence with impunity is severe but scale unresolved. D1's care denial killed someone. Hmm. I'll keep D1 0.45, D5 0.52 — reasonable, D1 lower because tier-1 institutional exposure applies to every outed visitor (wards, facilities, searches), while D5's exposure is violence-driven with documented protections and acceptance in hubs.
